newsitem.title: UK: Alcoholic drinks cited for violating UK guidelines.
newsitem.headline: Alcoholic drinks cited for violating UK guidelines.

text.p: Three alcoholic drinks violated British marketing guidelines by inferring that consumption could boost sexual prowess and by using dangerous images, an industry watchdog group said on Friday.
The Portman Group, a watchdog organisation set up by drinks companies, said TNT Liquid Dynamite, Purple Passion and Dogs Bollocks all violated marketing guidelines.
TNT Liquid Dynamite, a strong white cider marketed in the UK by Round Imports, broke guidelines because its packaging was reminiscent of a stick of dynamite, the Portman Group said.

Dogs Bollocks, a beer marketed by Wychwood Brewery Co Ltd, broke the marketing code by implying sexual prowess. The drink's strapline, "Dangerously Drinkable," also suggested danagerous behaviour, and its cartoon imagery was likely to appeal predominantly to those under the legal drinking age of 18, the watchdog group said.

Purple Passion, one of the highly sweetened, fruit-flavoured drinks known as "alcopops," broke guidelines because the phrase "testi coolz" on its packing inferred the product might boost sexual prowess, the Portman Group said.
The Portman Group also said it has named a complaints panel to handle protests about marketing in the industry. The new independent panel will be headed by former Banking Ombudsman Laurence Shurman.

"The new panel will sharpen the code's teeth," Jean Coussins, director of the Portman Group, said. "We're also doing our best to help drinks companies to comply with the code before new products hit shops, pubs and clubs through an advisory service.
"There is no excuse for irresponsible marketing," Coussins added.
